function: DQN agents set RIS row phase shifts, stream and modulation of semantic parts, and RIS-row usage, rewarded by accuracy, MSE or sum rate. pp. 3, 5, 8
system: 2x2 MIMO (4x4 for two users), two passive reflecting RISs with row-wise phase control, 1,024-subcarrier OFDM, Rician channel; carrier band not stated. pp. 3, 5, 9
method: Reinforcement learning: dense-layer DQN agents trained offline (1280 images, 100 epochs) then fine-tuned online; semantic CNN transceiver pretrained end-to-end and fixed. pp. 6-8
data_channel: Custom Rician channel (LoS/NLoS power ratio 10, 2 taps) with a user moving in a 10x10 m area and two RISs; OxfordPets and CamVid images. p. 9
test_conditions: Agents trained offline on 1280 known images (two RISs, one user), then fine-tuned online as the user moves, the direct link blocks and user requirements change. pp. 8-11
baselines: Learned: RL-Rate (conventional sum-rate reward), multi-armed bandit RIS control [23]; non-learned: JPEG+LDPC image transmission; also 0-RIS variants. pp. 9-10
metrics: Object classification accuracy (ACC, VGG-based), image MSE, average number of RIS rows used, angular offset to the optimal phase shift, convergence time. pp. 7-13
complexity: none; only convergence in time slots and about 5 s of simulated time for the slowest agent. p. 13
q1_support: p. 9: "we employ the Rician channel model with a delay spread of L = 2", with a position-dependent LoS and Gaussian NLoS. Custom simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 8: "the agents are fine-tuned to adapt to the changing channel environment and user requirements"; Fig. 10 (p. 11) and Fig. 14 (p. 13) show adaptation after a requirement change (RL-MSE trained from RL-ACC).
q3_support: p. 9: "Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB) [23], and other conventional methods such as JPEG+LDPC coding" are compared in Table I on ACC and MSE: JPEG+LDPC is non-learned, MAB [23] is an earlier learned RIS controller.
q4_support: p. 13: "the slowest method takes about 5 seconds to converge" is a convergence time in simulated time slots; no complexity order, operation or parameter count, or computing runtime is given.
q5_support: p. 9: "The OxfordPets dataset [40], comprising 6,390 training images and 1,000 testing images, is used"; these are image datasets of the learning task, the channel is self-simulated, and no code or data link is given.
notes: Included: the DQN agents set the RIS phase shifts (area 3); semantic image coding is the application and its transceiver is pretrained and fixed. q3 rests on JPEG+LDPC (non-learned, not an RIS algorithm) and MAB [23] (learned); RL-Rate is the authors' own variant. q4 is 0 because convergence in time slots is not computational cost. Table I and figure legends were read from the page images (pp. 9-10).
